capabilities.notes: Owned lifecycle and bounded join; successful native submission is not a connected callback. Mixing raw runtime ownership is unsupported.
Explicit service-wide string/numeric identity; token privileges must match.
Only combinations that preserve owned observers, lifecycle and publication contracts are supported.
Parameters are passed to the native SDK; a valid JSON object is not proof of option support.
Independent send/receive PCM formats; integral-millisecond input, caller/native timing limits, copied receive frames.
Codec packets with named native codec IDs, SendEvenIfEmpty, explicit metadata and OpusMultiChannel with 3–8 channels; native codec support is conditional.
WaitPCM is a sent-byte/wall-clock estimate, not native drain or peer playback acknowledgement.
Validated compact and explicitly padded/cropped CPU layouts; no GPU/hardware handles are accepted.
Encoded frames only; peer/native codec availability remains conditional.
High-level methods cover normal publication/subscription; manual subscription must be configured explicitly.
RTC data streams are distinct from RTM; local submission does not confirm recipient processing.
Owned observer delivery and bounded copied queues; detailed callback decisions/configuration are classified separately.
Extension-dependent external APM; pinned Linux archive lacks AINS, so initialization can fail.
Bounded request waits and ownership; cancellation stops waiting and does not roll back submitted native actions.
Messaging and user targets with explicit options; feature entitlements and peer delivery require integration checks.
Presence queries and copied state; legacy WhoNow/WhereNow map to equivalent query families rather than duplicated high-level method names.
Revision zero is forwarded unchanged; use explicit revisions and account for asynchronous completion.
High-level operations default to no native acquisition retry; AcquireLockWithOptions permits explicit retry with documented late outcomes.
Requires native/project history support and history-enabled publishing; binary messages are copied by explicit length.
Owned stream channels and partial-subscription results. Stream join/renew uses RTC tokens.
Copied event payloads with bounded drop-newest queue; request correlation is separate from that queue.
Borrowed native handles cannot outlive the callback, replace owned handlers, or release owned objects.
Pinned C callback ABI overrides unsafe upstream Go signatures; not drop-in source compatibility.
Slice callbacks retain every native array element; method status/request-ID fixes are listed individually in exceptions.
Binary metadata is copied; audio profile/scenario and volume indication keep native behavior and limits.
Exposes native keyframe requests, encoder configuration and simulcast; no claim that native codecs accept every configuration.
Received-audio VAD v2 is separate from standalone native VAD and external APM; 16 kHz mono per-user receive constraints apply.
Copied native encryption configuration is applied during setup; interoperability and privileges need a live check.
High-level entry points exist with and without avcodec; actual decoding requires optional FFmpeg libraries. Acceptance does not report asynchronous decode/send completion.
Pure packet helpers are retained in raw package; they are not an end-to-end SEI transport guarantee.

Media player, RTMP publishing and device APIs are not in official Go v2.6.5. C++-only RTM stream parameters/timestamps and hardware-video marshalling lack corresponding pinned Go/C surfaces; these are not lost official-Go methods. Extensions/codecs remain conditional.
Audience promotion lazily creates configured tracks; demotion unpublishes them. Native hook partial operations are reconciled with current role/publication state.

Idle mode retires observers/Go resources immediately and delays native handle destruction until service drains it. Local access point applies before first Connect. Extension success depends on installed native libraries.

Nil fallback rejects the synchronous native suggestion; fixed/recommended policy is atomic. Queued events preserve elapsed time, copied video-track information and requested fallback decision, not success confirmation.

Synchronous accept/reject hooks receive isolated copies; queued observations remain independent, including rejected frames. PCM edits copy back only at read/write mixed/local points on acceptance; before-mixing stays read-only. Panics reject and emit CallbackPanic. Hooks must return promptly and avoid lifecycle reentry.

CPU raw/array only, explicit pixel stride/crop/color/alpha and I420/NV12/NV21/I422/I010/RGBA/BGRA. Native preview/codec support remains conditional; texture/EGL/CVPixelBuffer/D3D handles are rejected.

All named native codec IDs are exposed; OpusMultiChannel accepts 3–8 channels. Encoded-video transport accepts 8 codec IDs; SEI insertion and optional decoding remain H264/H265-only. Enum acceptance is not live codec support.
Controls connection-owned tracks under lifecycle lock; missing tracks fail, void native setter success means invocation only, and clearing a local queue cannot recall received media.
Frame send preserves explicit sample/capture/presentation fields. Processor input/output are independent; DisableAPM requires VAD. Stats are durations, not flush acknowledgement.

Standalone mono/stereo classifiers accept exactly 10 ms of 16 kHz PCM16. TelemetryVAD is a Go segmenter using native telemetry, not an independent classifier. Detectors own resources and copied selected speech.
Synchronous owned H264/H265→I420 and Opus→PCM helpers require avcodec/FFmpeg. Default constructors return ErrUnsupported; Close discards pending output. No upstream flush API.

Default uses string identity without Native; IdentityDefault preserves Native.UseStringUserId when provided. Explicit modes override it. Typed configs deep-copy mutable input and preserve native timing/proxy/encryption/private options.

Presence-only subscriptions and omitted user IDs are explicit. Retry can continue after caller cancellation/timeout; opt-in result events expose later native outcomes, which the application must reconcile.

All 46 native callbacks have managed handlers: 8 unsolicited and 38 typed results. Opt-in copied result notifications include late/repeated outcomes without changing request completion or requiring lossless event delivery.

Pinned C enum names and typed error reasons are exposed. Header-based enum tests verify values independently of this official-Go snapshot; new C-surface names are additions beyond the official Go baseline.

Low-level constructors, conversions, utility/resource methods and advanced calls remain directly accessible with manual ownership. Selected invalid-handle paths are tested, not every callable or live behavior. Higher-level equivalents do not promise identical callback/lifecycle semantics.
